# Plan (muse-spark-1.3-contributor, medium)

## Goal

Give the AI's beam a look at enemy-aimed plays by interleaving each `round_robin` source's variants enemy-first (enemy hero first), instead of listing the chooser's own targets first. Done means: an enemy-aimed Burn sorts inside `AI_BUDGET.branching` (6) in the issue's crowded case, ally-only and targetless sources keep `legal_actions` order, a new tactics puzzle needs an attack plus below-root face burns and fails without the fix, the tier-2 move-order paragraph in `docs/polish/3-ai.md` describes the interleave, and the AI suite plus the smoke gate are green with before/after numbers in the PR.

## Files to touch

| File | New/change | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `crates/ai/src/candidates.rs` | change | Add `Selection` to the `jackioh_engine` import; add `FirstAim` enum plus `first_aim` and `interleave_enemy_first` fns before `round_robin`; `round_robin` gains a `seat: PlayerId` param, reorders each source's variants, and its doc comment grows one sentence; update the call in `candidate_actions_in`. |
| `crates/ai/tests/ai/search.rs` | change | New `mod target_interleave` with two tests (names in Tests). |
| `crates/ai/tests/ai/puzzles.rs` | change | One new test in `mod tactics_b18` (name in Tests). |
| `docs/polish/3-ai.md` | change | Tier-2 move-order bullet 2 (lines 523-524) gains the interleave sentence (exact text in step 7). |

Must not touch: `crates/ai/src/reply.rs` (the optional `known_play` early-return is deliberately left out), `crates/engine/`, `crates/cards/`, `crates/server/`, `apps/web/`, anything under `.github/`, `.harness/`, `bot/`. Governing spec: SPEC §9.9 (`spec/09-architecture.md:134-159`) is read, not changed; §10.6 `sides_for` and §8 Conventions are background only. No ruling note: move order is implementation detail, following the #1014/#1038 precedent, and the rejected plain enemy-first sort is what `scorer.rs::target_rank` already does for its own different purpose.

## Steps

1. Read SPEC §9.9, `crates/ai/src/candidates.rs:217-265` and `:370-414`, `crates/ai/src/reply.rs:287-305` (`aim_of`, the pattern to copy), and `crates/engine/src/subsystems/scorer.rs:394-413` (the contrast: a plain enemy-first sort, rejected here because it would bury own-side buffs and heals).
2. Add the tests first (TDD, so no worktree is needed to prove they fail on main). In `crates/ai/tests/ai/search.rs` add `mod target_interleave` with the two tests from Tests below. Run `cargo test -p jackioh-ai --test ai target_interleave`: the Burn test must fail (first enemy-aimed Burn at index 6, bound is 6), the order-preservation test must pass.
3. Add the puzzle test from Tests below to `mod tactics_b18` in `crates/ai/tests/ai/puzzles.rs`. Run `cargo test -p jackioh-ai --test ai burn_to_the_face_below_the_root_after_charge`: it must fail with the enemy hero at 14. Decision: the puzzle wins with face burns, not a blocker kill, because a blocker killable by one burn is also killable burn-first at the root (damage commutes), which the unfixed code already finds; crowding the root past 20 with a second Burn plus Fig of Life (cost 3, side-any heal, never usefully played at full health, so it crowds without competing) forces the win below the root.
4. In `crates/ai/src/candidates.rs`, add `Selection` to the existing `use jackioh_engine::{...}` list (after `Row`). Then, between the `Source` struct and `round_robin`, add:
   ```rust
   /// Where one source variant's first target aims (#1062).
   #[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
   enum FirstAim {
       /// At the enemy hero.
       EnemyHero,
       /// At a card the enemy controls.
       EnemyCard,
       /// Anything else: no targets, an own-side target, a zone, hand or graveyard pick.
       Other,
   }
   ```
   and `fn first_aim(state: &GameState, seat: PlayerId, action: &ActionBody) -> FirstAim`, which reads `targets` off `Play`, `Activate` and `ActivatePower` (anything else is `Other`), returning `EnemyHero` for `Selection::Hero` naming `seat.opponent()`, `EnemyCard` for `Selection::Instance` whose `find_instance` has `controller == seat.opponent()`, else `Other`. Copy the match shape from `reply.rs::aim_of`.
5. Add `fn interleave_enemy_first(state: &GameState, seat: PlayerId, variants: &[ActionBody]) -> Vec<ActionBody>`: stable-split each source's variants into enemy-hero, other-enemy, and rest (all in `legal_actions` order), concatenate hero-first enemy groups, then emit e0, o0, e1, o1, …. An empty enemy group returns the input order exactly, which is what keeps targetless and own-side-only sources untouched. Decision: interleave rather than sort, so buffs and heals aimed own-side are never buried behind enemy targets.
6. Change `fn round_robin(state: &GameState, actions: &[ActionBody])` to take `seat: PlayerId`, run each source's `variants` through `interleave_enemy_first` right after the grouping loop, and update the call to `round_robin(state, seat, &plays)`. Extend its doc comment with: "Inside one source's variants, enemy-aimed ones interleave first, enemy hero first (#1062), so a board of own targets cannot crowd the enemy's out of the beam." Run `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-ai --all-targets -- -D warnings`, then the two new tests plus `cargo test -p jackioh-ai` in full.
7. In `docs/polish/3-ai.md`, replace bullet 2's tail `each round by \`effectiveCost\` descending ·` with `each round by \`effectiveCost\` descending; inside one source's variants the enemy-aimed ones (first target the enemy hero or a card the enemy controls, enemy hero first) interleave with the rest enemy-first, so a board of own targets cannot crowd the enemy's out of the beam (#1062) ·`.
8. Run `cargo jackioh gate` on the branch. For the before numbers, `scripts/worktree.sh base-gate b26a7430c3bf8d8c2ef0e13bc8a5c067f05e2e34`, run `cargo jackioh gate` there, then remove that worktree. Record wins per matchup and the perf gate timing both sides.
9. If any existing AI test's pinned decision moves (candidates order feeds `lethal_moves` and `reply.rs::known_play`'s top 8 too), do not edit the test to fit: verify the new decision wins or holds the same outcome class, update the expectation minimally only then, and name each such test in the PR with why the new decision is at least as good.

## Tests
